symbols.name: chunk width
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two address chunks.
symbols.quote: Fast address-chunk interchange swaps two disjoint $u$-bit address fields of an array with $V$ entries (volume) in time $O(Vu^\tau)$

symbols.name: volume
symbols.meaning: The number of entries of the array.
symbols.quote: Fast address-chunk interchange swaps two disjoint $u$-bit address fields of an array with $V$ entries (volume) in time $O(Vu^\tau)$

symbols.name: time exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed exponent below 1 in the time bound, 1-2^{-50}.
symbols.quote: with $\tau=1-2^{-50}$ fixed.

symbols.name: radix

symbols.quote: With radix-$q$ digits, $q$ a fixed prime, let $H,D$ be the chunk values.

symbols.quote: With radix-$q$ digits, $q$ a fixed prime, let $H,D$ be the chunk values.

symbols.name: chunk digits
symbols.meaning: The number of radix-q digits in each chunk.
symbols.quote: Let chunks have $e=m^k$ digits ($m$ fields, $k$ levels), each field $b=e/m$ digits, so $H,D$ are vectors over $\mathbb Z/q^b\mathbb Z$.

symbols.quote: Let chunks have $e=m^k$ digits ($m$ fields, $k$ levels), each field $b=e/m$ digits, so $H,D$ are vectors over $\mathbb Z/q^b\mathbb Z$.

symbols.name: levels

symbols.name: frame permutation
symbols.meaning: The address permutation moving the entry at (H,D) to (H+MD,D).
symbols.quote: A [frame](array-frames.md) at a vertex with matrix $M$ is the address permutation $\Phi_M$, $(H,D)\mapsto(H+MD,D)$

symbols.quote: A [frame](array-frames.md) at a vertex with matrix $M$ is the address permutation $\Phi_M$

symbols.name: cost per volume
symbols.meaning: A uniform upper bound on time divided by logical volume at width m^k.
symbols.quote: With $F_k$ the bound on time per unit volume at width $m^k$

symbols.name: chunk level
symbols.meaning: The least integer with m^{k'} at least e, the recursion depth for width e.
symbols.quote: Put $k'=\lceil\log_m e\rceil$ and let $\rho=\lceil k'\log W/(2\log q)\rceil$ be the number of top digits interchanged first

symbols.name: high digits
symbols.meaning: The number of top digits of each chunk interchanged first.
symbols.quote: Put $k'=\lceil\log_m e\rceil$ and let $\rho=\lceil k'\log W/(2\log q)\rceil$ be the number of top digits interchanged first

symbols.name: row range
symbols.meaning: The range of the row field formed by the two high parts.
symbols.quote: Joining them, the high parts form a row field of range $R=q^{2\rho}\ge W^{k'}$ before both remaining chunks.

symbols.name: piece count
symbols.meaning: The number of pieces of width m^j in the base-m expansion of e minus rho.
symbols.quote: Write $e-\rho=\sum_{j=0}^{k'} a_jm^j$, $0\le a_j<m$, and interchange corresponding pieces ($a_j$ pieces of width $m^j$) by the power-width case.

relations.quote: Each shear is performed by [Matrix shear by triangular factorization](matrix-shear.md): rank $\alpha$ costs $\alpha$ interchanges of $b$-digit fields
Each stream has volume $V/W$ and row count divisible by $W^{k-1}$; streams are split and merged by [stream scans](stream-ops.md).
With $F_k$ the bound on time per unit volume at width $m^k$, $F_0=O(1)$ and $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$, so it satisfies the recurrence of [Recursive power saving](rank-recurrence.md).

derivations.quote:
each on volume $V/W$; other work costs $O(V)$. With $F_k$ the bound on time per unit volume at width $m^k$, $F_0=O(1)$ and $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$, so it satisfies the recurrence of [Recursive power saving](rank-recurrence.md).

Then $F_k=O(\sum_{j=0}^k a^j)$, $a=s/W<m^\tau$. If $a\le1$, the sum is at most $k+1=O(m^{k\tau})$. If $a>1$, it is $O(a^k)$ with $a^k<m^{k\tau}$. So $F_k=O(e^\tau)$.

Put $k'=\lceil\log_m e\rceil$ and let $\rho=\lceil k'\log W/(2\log q)\rceil$ be the number of top digits interchanged first, so $q^{2\rho}\ge W^{k'}$. Joining them, the high parts form a row field of range $R=q^{2\rho}\ge W^{k'}$ before both remaining chunks. Pad with zero rows to $R'=W^{k'}\lceil R/W^{k'}\rceil<2R$ rows.

Write $e-\rho=\sum_{j=0}^{k'} a_jm^j$, $0\le a_j<m$, and interchange corresponding pieces ($a_j$ pieces of width $m^j$) by the power-width case. The cost $O(V)\sum_j a_jm^{j\tau}=O(Ve^\tau)$ is geometric since $a_j<m$ and $m^{k'}<me$. Padding $[2^u]$ to $[q^e]$ costs a fixed factor and gives $O(Vu^\tau)$
